newsitem.title: JAPAN: Refiner General Sekiyu says profits fall sharply.
newsitem.headline: Refiner General Sekiyu says profits fall sharply.

text.p: Japanese refiner General Sekiyu KK said on Monday that surging costs stemming from rising crude prices and lower product prices battered its profits in the first half of this business year.
"The main reason for the drop in operating profits was poor refining margins," senior managing director Nobuyuki Toyama told reporters.
General Sekiyu, owned 49 percent by Exxon Corp, reported a parent current profit of 4.72 billion yen in the six months to September 30, down 45.3 percent from the same period a year earlier.
Current profit is pre-tax, including losses or gains on investments.
Costs to produce gasoline during the six-month period rose by about 2.8 yen per litre from a year earlier, while the wholesale price of gasoline fell by 5.3 yen per litre, Toyama said.
Production costs have soared because of rising global crude prices and the yen's weakness against the dollar.
Retail prices were depressed by price competition among gasoline station operators, sparked by the liberalisation of oil product imports this April, General Sekiyu said.
Prices of other oil products, such as gas oil and kerosene, have also failed to keep up with rising crude prices because of consumers' opposition to a rise in prices, it said.
The higher costs offset an increase in the company's sales volume of oil products.

Toyama said sales of oil products in the six-month period edged up 1.8 percent from a year earlier to 7.40 million kilolitres, reflecting good demand for gasoline and gas oil, which are used as fuel, and kerosene, which is used for heating.
The amount of crude processed by the Japanese oil industry betweeb April and September increased 1.1 percent from the same period a year earlier, General Sekiyu said.
However, the industry's refinery operating rates dropped by 0.5 point to 74.8 percent because of an increase in refining capacity, it said.
